analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and the `stop` parameter row (head line 2126). The row now says Gemma 4 and `<think>` parsers exclude reasoning spans and tool-call spans from stop-string matching per request (`ReasoningStopScope`). The supplied units are unchanged base excerpts (lines 2465-3234) with no modifications, so I reviewed them as context only. The patch changes no executable code, keys, attestation, encryption, routing or authorization. Threat IDs I considered: T-008 (plaintext on encryption failure), T-041 (prefix cache) and TB-002/TB-007. None is affected by a documentation edit.

The stop-sequence scoping behaviour is described only in documentation. I could not see the implementation in `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift` or `ReasoningStopScope`. Excluding reasoning and tool spans from stop matching could affect output truncation or how tool-call arguments are handled, but that is a correctness matter and not an established security regression. It is not covered by any supplied evidence, so I flag nothing. The unchanged text I read in the supplied excerpts (cache, sidecar, hold, cluster, media admission) is pre-existing and not restated. The remaining open question is whether the actual code matches the new description. Per the instructions this is recorded here as an unverified contract and not raised as a finding.
